newsitem.title: INDONESIA: FORECAST-Indonesia Citra Marga sees higher net.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Indonesia Citra Marga sees higher net.

text.p: Indonesian toll-road operator Citra Marga Nusaphala Persada, controlled by President Suharto's eldest daughter Siti Hardiyanti Rukmana, expects net profit to rise in 1997 and is planning a bond issue in February.
Citra corporate finance manager Ilham Wardhana Siregar told an analysts' meeting on Wednesday that the company's net profit was expected to increase to 145 billion rupiah in 1997.
He said the company was on track to post a net profit of 123 billion rupiah this year, up from 94 billion in 1995.
"Based on the 1996 third quarter performance, we believe we can achieve a net profit of 123 billion rupiah this year," he said.
The company posted net profit of 93.21 billion rupiah in the first nine months of this year, compared with 66.7 billion in the same 1995 period.
"Based on this performance, we project 1997 net profit at 145 billion rupiah."
Analysts said the forecasts were within their expectations.
"It is within my target. I expect Citra Marga to book a net profit of 145.4 billion rupiah for 1997," Boedi Pranoto, analyst with PT Usaha Bersama Sekuritas, said.
As of November 28, the market concensus for Citra Marga's 1997 net profit is 140.3 billion rupiah. For 1996 it is 123.3 billion rupiah.
Siregar said the company was projected to post net profit of 284 billion rupiah in 2000.

"Considering the traffic volume growth of eight percent per year and increases of 500 rupiah in Jakarta toll tariffs every 2-1/2 years, our net profit is targeted to reach 284 billion rupiah in the year 2000," he said.
He said Citra had submitted a proposal to the government to raise tariffs for Jakarta inner city toll roads by at least 500 rupiah every 2-1/2 years.
"We have submitted the proposal but the decision itself is (in) the government's hands," he said.
Siregar also said that Citra was planning a one-for-one rights issue in the third quarter of 1997. He said the rights issue was subject to shareholders' approval.
He said the firm would also issue a $100 million Eurobond and a 250-billion rupiah bond in February 1997.
Siregar said the Eurobond would carry an interest rate of 8.25 percent and mature in five years, while the Indonesian bond would have an interest rate of 17 percent and mature in seven years.
"We are going to issue the bonds in February 1997," he said, adding that proceeds will be used to finance the construction of a toll road in Surabaya, East Java costing 1.3 trillion rupiah.
Construction of the 24-km Waru-Tanjung Perak road would start by the second quarter of 1997 and be completed by the second quarter of 2001.
Citra shares rose 75 rupiah to 1,975 rupiah ahead of the analysts' meeting on expectation of positive news, but closed at 1,950 rupiah on profit taking on turnover of 1.5 million shares.
